name: Ring USD
oneLiner: USDR is Ring Protocol's centrally managed synthetic dollar minted against protocol-controlled crypto collateral, with no public redemption route documented.
collateral: Ring protocol crypto collateral and strategy assets managed through the protocol reserve system
pegMechanism: RUSD is collateralized by a Protocol Controlled Value (PCV) reserve funded through bonding-curve issuance; PCV is allocated to liquidity and the token can be over- or under-collateralized depending on reserve conditions; no holder-exercisable redemption route is source-reviewed for Pharos backstop scoring

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Yes retained: reviewed metadata indicates a direct issuer, admin, proxy, pause, burn, or upgrade control surface beyond reserve-only exposure.

reserves.name: Ring protocol crypto collateral and liquidity positions

notices.title: Redemption backstop not modeled
notices.message: Ring Protocol materials describe protocol liquidity controls, but Pharos has not source-reviewed a holder-exercisable redemption route for backstop scoring.

mintAuthority.summary: Ring USD (USDR) is a Fei-fork ERC20Burnable whose Minter-role holders can mint to any address uncapped; minting is gated by Ring Protocol's Core access-control contract, with supply primarily sourced through PCV bonding-curve issuance.

controls.label: USDR Minter role (Core-gated)
controls.capDescription: Minting and burning to any address are uncapped and accessible to any contract granted the Minter/Burner role by Ring Protocol's Core.
controls.evidence: Etherscan read of the verified USDR token (name 'Ring USD', symbol 'USDR') shows ERC20Burnable + CoreRef: Minter role can mint to any address with no cap; Burner role can burn; a Guardian/Governor can trigger emergency mode and the Core admin updates the Core reference.

controls.label: Ring Protocol Core / Governor-Guardian
controls.evidence: The Core contract assigns Minter/Burner roles; the Governor/Guardian can grant roles, manage the Core address, and trigger emergency mode, so the Core admin can authorize new minters at will.

review.evidence: Ring USD is a Fei-Protocol-style stablecoin (CoreRef access control, PCV bonding-curve issuance). The on-chain verified token confirms Minter-role holders can mint uncapped to any address, with role assignment controlled by the Core/Governor. No holder-exercisable redemption is documented; supply expansion is fully admin/role controlled.
review.sourceFreeRationale: Token role model confirmed via Etherscan verified source read; the concrete Core/Governor admin address (EOA vs multisig) and current Minter-role holders were not enumerated.
unresolvedQuestions: Enumerate the current Minter-role holders and resolve whether the Ring Core Governor/Guardian is an EOA, multisig, or timelock before raising confidence.
